name: New Hampshire

law.name: New Hampshire repealed its athlete agent law in 2023.

summary: No state license. Follow federal SPARTA rules and each school's rules.

steps.detail: New Hampshire repealed its athlete agent law in 2023.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Warn the athlete in writing that signing could affect their eligibility
steps.detail: This is required by federal law (SPARTA) in every state.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Federal law bans pre-dating or post-dating it.

steps.text: Make sure the athlete tells their school about the deal
steps.detail: Most schools and state NIL laws require athletes to disclose NIL deals.

steps.text: Never make false promises or give gifts or money to recruit athletes
steps.detail: This is a federal SPARTA rule.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: "No law" is based on a secondary 50-state survey (Leave Your Agent, checked 2026-10-13). Confirm with the state legislature.
